basis: Congenital skin and hair depigmentation; white eyebrows and eyelashes do not establish ocular damage. Hearing and neurologic abnormalities occur in under 30%.
Osteochondrosis of the metatarsal head with structural bone and joint damage.
Degeneration of lumbar intervertebral disks; direct neurologic damage is not established across the disease.
Molar tooth malformation and developmental delay in 13/13; strabismus in 5/13 supports ocular involvement. Renal insufficiency in 2/13 is below threshold.
Benign tumor arising in the Bartholin gland, a reproductive organ outside the defined axes.
Skeletal dysplasia and oligodontia with abnormal incisors jointly define the syndrome; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Glial tumor involving the corpus callosum of the brain.
Substance dependence is outside the axes; associated organ diseases are separate diagnoses and vary by substance.
Mitochondrial metabolic defect; developmental delay 2/3, cardiomyopathy/heart failure 1/3 and retinal degeneration 1/3. Small cohort; cholelithiasis is a separate disease.
Isolated inverted nipples affect the breast, which is outside the defined axes.
Lysosomal storage disorder defined by congenital neurodegeneration, microcephaly and neonatal epilepsy.
Mediastinal smooth muscle tumor; mediastinal soft tissue lies outside the defined axes, and no lung, airway or vascular origin is specified.
Familial Behcet-like autoinflammation with characteristic recurrent oral mucosal ulceration; other organ damage varies across subtypes.
Hereditary degeneration of motor pathways causes spastic paraplegia; additional organ abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Persistent inflammation of the bile ducts; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not specified.
Inhaled mineral dust directly causes interstitial lung injury and fibrosis.
Extragonadal germ cell malignancy originating in the mediastinum, outside the defined organs; thoracic location alone does not establish pulmonary origin.
Ichthyosis and sparse eyebrows define the skin phenotype; skeletal findings lack frequencies supporting common involvement.
Congenital structural cleft of the nose; the pulmonary axis explicitly includes the nose.
One reported case: severe developmental delay/callosal dysplasia, renal hypoplasia/aminoaciduria and fixed contractures, each 1/1. Hepatomegaly alone does not prove liver damage.
Inherited isolated restrictive cardiomyopathy directly affects the myocardium.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy with joint contractures. Skin findings occur in under 30%; hypoventilation reflects muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Centrofacial lentiginosis with neurodevelopmental impairment, including intellectual disability, characterizes this syndrome.
Immune-mediated peripheral nerve and nerve-root injury; respiratory weakness and autonomic symptoms do not establish direct lung or heart damage.
Autoimmune arthritis, neutropenia and splenomegaly define the syndrome; subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules occur in 80-99%. Respiratory and ear infections are separate diseases.
